nodes.label: hosted-anthropic Experiment Profile
nodes.rationale: The deliberate opposite of the default: every component hosted, and the only configuration in which citations are verified against the source text rather than asserted by the model. Exists as a quality ceiling to measure the local stack against — specifically to quantify qwen3:8b's numeric-fidelity gap. claude-opus-5 with effort low and cache_system_prompt, claude-haiku-4-5 as fast_llm, OpenAI text-embedding-3-large, chunk 1200/150, 40 candidates → top 8, max_tokens 4096.

nodes.label: 3072-Dimension Embedding Caveat
nodes.rationale: text-embedding-3-large is 3072-dimensional, exceeding pgvector's 2000-dimension HNSW limit, so the migration leaves the column unindexed and vector search falls back to an exact scan. It also needs its own database (osc_hosted3072) because vector width is fixed when the chunks table is created. This is the exact configuration that would have aborted migration before the conditional-index fix.

nodes.label: Hosted Models Lift the Prompt Budget
nodes.rationale: Hosted models are served with a large context, so the prompt budget the local 4096-token deployment is constrained to no longer applies — chunk_size rises 900→1200, overlap 120→150, candidates 30→40, top_k 5→8 and max_tokens 1500→4096. A concrete demonstration that the local tuning is a deployment constraint, not a retrieval finding.
nodes.norm_label: hosted models lift the prompt budget

nodes.label: local-only Experiment Profile
nodes.rationale: Local without Ollama embeddings: sentence-transformers in-process plus a cross-encoder reranker. The default profile is already fully local via Ollama, so this profile exists specifically to exercise the second local embedding path and the reranker. Needs pip install -e '.[local]'.

nodes.label: BGE Asymmetric Query Prefix
nodes.rationale: bge is asymmetric: queries expect the instruction prefix 'Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: ' while documents do not. Encoding both sides identically would degrade retrieval, so the prefix is a provider option rather than something business logic knows about.

nodes.label: 384-Dimension Database Separation
nodes.rationale: bge-small-en-v1.5 is 384-dimensional against nomic-embed-text's 768. The chunks table fixes its vector width at migration time, so this profile needs its own database (osc_local384) and a full re-index; it cannot share one with the default profile.

nodes.label: cross_encoder Reranker (ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2)
nodes.rationale: The only profile that enables reranking. It is the exercise path for the reranker seam that the default profile leaves as noop, and the configuration whose unbounded negative logits motivated moving min_score to first-stage scores.

nodes.label: Development PostgreSQL + pgvector Service
nodes.rationale: Deliberately optional: the reference development environment uses a natively installed PostgreSQL, so this file is a convenience and not a requirement. The application creates its own schema on first use, so the service only needs to exist. Has a pg_isready healthcheck and a named volume for data.

nodes.label: pgvector Image Tag Pinning Intent
nodes.rationale: The comment states the image is pinned by digest because pg16 is a moving tag and an unannounced pgvector or server upgrade underneath a populated volume is not something to discover during an incident. The actual image line is `pgvector/pgvector:pg16` — the tag, not a digest — so the stated intent and the config disagree. PROJECT_STATUS.md §8 and §14 corroborate this: the digest is explicitly listed as not pinned, deprioritised because the compose file is now a secondary path.

nodes.label: OSC Knowledge Assistant Web UI
nodes.rationale: Deliberately one self-contained file with no build step and no framework, imported by nothing in the backend, so the whole UI can be replaced by swapping the single file. A richer client is the expected path.

nodes.label: renderSources
nodes.rationale: Re-renders the whole source list on every citation event rather than patching one node, because a citation can arrive for any already-rendered source and full replace is cheaper to reason about than diffing.

nodes.label: Health check status banner
nodes.rationale: Surfaces llm provider/model, embedding model, vector store provider and retrieval strategy from GET /api/health so the operator can see which configuration answered a question without reading server config.

nodes.label: SSE chat stream protocol (sources/delta/citation/complete/error)
nodes.rationale: Frames are separated by a blank line and a partial frame stays buffered, so the client can decode arbitrary chunk boundaries from the reader without a framing library.

nodes.label: Complete event is authoritative
nodes.rationale: The one rule worth preserving on a rewrite: the complete event replaces whatever streamed. When it reports an abstention the client must discard already-rendered delta text and drop the source list, because the assistant declined to answer and streamed fragments would read as a partial answer.

nodes.label: Conversation history deliberately not sent
nodes.rationale: Query rewriting is disabled by default, so sending history would make a follow-up retrieve against an unresolved reference. Single-turn requests keep retrieval grounded until rewriting exists.

nodes.label: Grounded answer / abstention contract
nodes.rationale: Answers are generated only from retrieved sources with citations; if the corpus lacks the answer the assistant says so rather than guessing. The UI states this up front so users read an abstention as correct behaviour, not failure.

nodes.label: Add-on Tier Pricing
nodes.rationale: Quantity-tier prices are computed from merchant cost inputs plus margin rather than entered as literal prices, so a reseller with only a blank item cost can use one cost parameter and one margin while a branded-goods merchant can layer setup, decoration and shipping costs into the same tier ladder without manual per-tier arithmetic.

nodes.label: Cost Parameters and Profit Margins (up to 4 costs, 2 margins)
nodes.norm_label: cost parameters and profit margins (up to 4 costs, 2 margins)

nodes.label: Per-Variant Quantity Range Evaluation
nodes.rationale: Every cart line is priced against its own variant quantity range instead of a cart-wide total, so a mixed multi-line wholesale order keeps each product on its correct tier (71 shirts on the 50-71 tier and 11 jumpers on the 6-11 tier simultaneously) without the buyer losing a bulk discount by mixing products.

nodes.label: Cart Discount
nodes.rationale: Tiering is expressed as multiple minimum-value rows with matching discount amounts rather than a scheduling or segmentation system; date scheduling and customer-tag conditions are explicitly deferred to a future release.

nodes.label: Combined Collection Quantity Discount Slabs
nodes.rationale: Quantity is summed per registered collection rather than across the whole cart, so registering several collections keeps their slabs independent; collection membership changes auto-update eligibility so merchants never re-declare rules after a merchandising change.

nodes.label: App-Created Discount Label
nodes.rationale: The label is the Shopify-side handle the app attaches discounts to; deleting it silently stops all discounts, which is why the documented recovery is to recreate the label and update rules rather than to reinstall.

nodes.label: Best Discount Tier Across Multiple Collections
nodes.rationale: When one product belongs to several registered collections the most favourable tier wins (20% from Collection A beats 10% from Collection B), so overlapping merchandising never penalises the buyer.
nodes.norm_label: best discount tier across multiple collections

nodes.label: Draft Order Processing
nodes.rationale: Checkout is intercepted and a Shopify Draft Order carrying the wholesale price is created, which avoids strikethrough pricing but means the cart page necessarily still shows Shopify's regular prices — wholesale pricing only becomes visible once the Draft Order exists at checkout. Current phase supports variant-level tier pricing only.

nodes.label: 15-Minute Invoice Reuse Window
nodes.rationale: Duplicate-click protection: if cart contents are unchanged the same Draft Order is reused for 15 minutes instead of minting a new one per click, preventing a flood of orphan draft orders.

nodes.label: Server-Side Wholesale Price Validation
nodes.rationale: All wholesale calculations are verified server-side because storefront-computed discounts are attacker-controllable; the customer must not be able to manipulate discount values.

nodes.label: Shopify Coupon Applied After Tier Discount
nodes.rationale: Coupons apply to the already-discounted Draft Order price, not the original product price ($30 - 10% tier = $27, then -$5 coupon = $22), so tier and coupon discounts compound in a defined order rather than both taking the list price as their base.
nodes.norm_label: shopify coupon applied after tier discount

nodes.label: CSV Export and Bulk Import of Variant Rules
nodes.rationale: Export is delivered by email rather than direct download, so the email notification address must be configured first; the exported CSV doubles as the sample template for bulk editing and re-import.
nodes.norm_label: csv export and bulk import of variant rules

nodes.label: Extra Fee
nodes.rationale: Surcharges (handling, packaging, COD, B2B service) are expressed as unlimited no-code rules with an Applies-To scope and slab conditions, and a priority/stacking setting decides whether concurrent rules stack or only one wins.

nodes.label: Free Gift
nodes.rationale: No coupon code is required — the gift is auto-added when the cart qualifies and shown as a discounted line so the customer can see it costs nothing; eligibility can be scoped to everyone, logged-in customers, or a specific tag.

nodes.label: Market-Based Offers
nodes.rationale: A market-specific offer outranks an All Markets offer for customers in that market, and two offers on the same market never stack — the better price wins. Testing is done with a test address or VPN plus guest checkout.

nodes.label: Order Limits
nodes.rationale: Limits are evaluated on the whole cart (total quantity or total amount) rather than per product, and the merchant chooses whether all conditions or any single condition triggers the limit.

nodes.label: Row-Level Then Order-Level Discount Ordering
nodes.rationale: Row-level discounts are computed and applied first; the order-level discount is then evaluated against the resulting final amount, so the two can stack but the order-level threshold is judged post-row-discount.

nodes.label: Priority of the Offers
nodes.rationale: Specificity decides: variant-level tier price beats product-level, which beats collection-level. This is why an offer can appear on only one variant — a variant rule is shadowing the product rule.

nodes.label: Offer List Drag-and-Drop Ordering
nodes.rationale: When a product sits in two collections with competing tier rules, precedence is the visual order of the Offer List rather than the best price — the merchant reorders by drag-and-drop to change which collection offer displays on the PDP.

nodes.label: Product and Collection Page Integration
nodes.rationale: Supports the BUY NOW button and third-party payment gateways; merchants may replace the pricing grid with a single discounted price. A single offer is capped at 10 collections, beyond which a separate offer is required.

nodes.label: Quick Order Form
nodes.rationale: SKU entry is manual and per-row (bulk/CSV upload is not yet available); entering a variant SKU targets that exact variant, and configured tiered pricing rules surface inside the form so buyers see quantity-based pricing while ordering.

nodes.label: B2B Registration Form
nodes.rationale: Built in four steps (title/description, primary contact, business details, custom fields) with per-field label, hint and validation, and surfaced on the storefront by adding its link as a Shopify Main menu item.

nodes.label: Email Notification Setup (three templates)
nodes.rationale: Three templates cover the approval workflow: request-submitted to the customer, request-received to the store owner, and approval notification when status moves pending to approved. Emails do not send at all until this is configured, which is the documented cause of 'why am I not receiving emails'.

nodes.label: Row Level Discount
nodes.rationale: Applied before shipping and tax so tax is computed on the true discounted base. Currently all-or-nothing across the cart (no selected vs non-selected product split), and tiering requires separate offers per threshold. Discounts recalculate when the cart drops below the minimum.

nodes.label: Tax Display
nodes.rationale: Display-only feature: it shows inclusive and exclusive prices on the PDP pricing grid per selected country and never changes what Shopify charges at checkout. Country-specific rates override the global rate, the countries need Shopify Markets configured, and the setting is global rather than per-product.

nodes.label: Theme Compatibility
nodes.rationale: Because themes vary, the app binds to the storefront through merchant-supplied element IDs/classes (Add to Cart, Checkout button, cart and mini cart) entered in the Wholesale Price app embed, rather than assuming a fixed DOM. A missing price grid on a customised PDP is diagnosed by checking whether the cart and checkout still price correctly.

nodes.label: Custom Price Grid App Block / App Embed
nodes.rationale: Enabled as a Shopify App Embed plus a Product-information block placed below Price. Conflicting third-party pricing apps are a known cause of the wholesale table not rendering.
nodes.norm_label: custom price grid app block / app embed

nodes.label: Tiered Pricing (collection, product and variant level)
nodes.rationale: One mechanism applied at three scopes (collection, product, variant), each gated by customer tag, and it also applies to orders placed by staff through Shopify admin so offline/rep orders price identically to storefront orders.
nodes.norm_label: tiered pricing (collection, product and variant level)

nodes.label: OSCP Wholesale B2B Pricing — Scenario Document
nodes.rationale: Maps every app feature to real-world merchant scenarios with acceptance criteria, and deliberately records out-of-scope scenarios in section 4 so that omissions read as decisions rather than oversights. Audience: PMs, junior devs, QA, merchant support.
nodes.norm_label: oscp wholesale b2b pricing — scenario document

nodes.label: FEAT-01 Quantity Break Pricing (SCN-001, SCN-002)
nodes.rationale: Two shapes are supported because merchants ask for different things: percentage-off for volume incentives, and fixed price per unit for manufacturers who want trade customers to see a predictable price ladder. Boundary quantities, downgrade on removal and per-variant independence are the load-bearing edge cases.

nodes.label: FEAT-02 Customer Tag Tier Pricing (SCN-003, SCN-004)
nodes.rationale: Lets one store serve retail and multiple B2B segments from one admin panel. Unresolved-by-design points that must be documented: overlapping tag rules (most favourable applies), logout mid-session removing the discount, and tag removal taking effect within one session refresh.
nodes.norm_label: feat-02 customer tag tier pricing (scn-003, scn-004)

nodes.label: FEAT-03 Markets-Based Pricing (SCN-005)
nodes.rationale: Region-specific discount structures reflect local market conditions and currency; when a market has no rule the system must fall back to the global rule or no discount rather than fail.

nodes.label: FEAT-04 Cart Level Discount (SCN-006, SCN-007)
nodes.rationale: Triggered by cart value or item count to raise average order value; must appear as its own summary line, be removed automatically when the cart drops below threshold, and have defined stacking behaviour against Shopify coupon codes.

nodes.label: FEAT-05 Order Limits Min/Max (SCN-008, SCN-009)
nodes.rationale: Blocks checkout outside the merchant's viable order window and must state the exact shortfall ('Add $70 more'). Boundary values are inclusive, min set to $0 disables the feature, and a min > max misconfiguration must warn the merchant rather than silently block every order.

nodes.label: FEAT-06 B2B Registration Form (SCN-010)
nodes.rationale: Accounts sit in 'pending' until the merchant approves and applies a customer tag, which is what gates wholesale pricing. Notification failure must not lose the submission, and repeat approval must be idempotent.

nodes.label: FEAT-07 Quick / Bulk Order Form (SCN-011)
nodes.rationale: Capped at 50 products per order. A bad row must not abort the batch: unknown or out-of-stock SKUs are flagged inline while valid rows still reach the cart, and duplicate SKUs are merged into one line.

nodes.label: FEAT-08 Tax Display by Country (SCN-012)
nodes.rationale: Consumers see tax-inclusive and VAT-registered businesses see tax-exclusive prices per country; when the country cannot be detected the store default must be used rather than showing nothing, and tax-exempt products render zero tax, not an error.

nodes.label: FEAT-09 Bulk CSV Import/Export (SCN-013)
nodes.rationale: Up to 200 variant-level rules per import. Invalid rows are reported by row number and reason while valid rows still import; repeated variants follow last-row-wins, and existing rules are overwritten rather than duplicated.

nodes.label: FEAT-10 Auto Order Tagging (SCN-014)
nodes.rationale: Product metafields (brand, warehouse) drive order tags so fulfilment routing needs no manual step. Tags are applied once even when two products trigger the same tag, are not rewritten if the metafield later changes, and survive cancellation for audit.

nodes.label: FEAT-11 Hide Shipping Methods (SCN-015)
nodes.rationale: Tag-gated shipping (e.g. Freight delivery for wholesale only) prevents retail misuse. Fail-safe requirement: hiding must never leave checkout with zero methods — at least one option or a clear message must remain.

nodes.label: FEAT-12 Personalised Email Notifications (SCN-016)
nodes.rationale: Merchant notified within 2 minutes of a registration, applicant gets a merge-field confirmation. Delivery is best-effort but capture is not: a bounced merchant address or an invalid applicant email still leaves the submission saved, and a missing merge field renders blank instead of crashing.

nodes.label: SCN-X01 Customer-Level Fixed Price per SKU (out of scope)
nodes.rationale: Not built: high implementation complexity and Shopify API limits on individual customer price overrides at scale. Revisit Q3. Tag-group pricing is the supported substitute.
nodes.norm_label: scn-x01 customer-level fixed price per sku (out of scope)

nodes.label: SCN-X02 Multiple Simultaneous Cart-Level Discount Rules (out of scope)
nodes.rationale: Not built: the cart discount engine supports exactly one rule; concurrent rules ($20 off plus 10% off) would require an architectural change. Revisit Q2.
nodes.norm_label: scn-x02 multiple simultaneous cart-level discount rules (out of scope)

nodes.label: SCN-X03 Net 30 / Net 60 Payment Terms (out of scope)
nodes.rationale: Not planned: outside the scope of a pricing app; belongs to a dedicated payment-terms app. Explicit scope boundary, not a backlog item.
nodes.norm_label: scn-x03 net 30 / net 60 payment terms (out of scope)

nodes.label: SCN-X04 Customer-Tag-Based Cart Discount (out of scope)
nodes.rationale: Planned future feature, not yet built: different cart thresholds per tag group. Scheduled for Q2 development.
nodes.norm_label: scn-x04 customer-tag-based cart discount (out of scope)

nodes.label: OSCP Wholesale B2B Pricing — Scenario Document (duplicate copy)
nodes.rationale: Byte-for-byte duplicate of OSCP_B2B_Scenario_Document-1_cb06f24b.md (same version 1.0 draft, same FEAT-01..FEAT-12 table, same SCN-001..SCN-016 scenarios and same SCN-X01..SCN-X04 out-of-scope decisions). Two converted copies of the same source docx exist in graphify-out/converted.
nodes.norm_label: oscp wholesale b2b pricing — scenario document (duplicate copy)

nodes.label: OSCP Wholesale B2B — Scenario Master (SCN-001..SCN-010)
nodes.rationale: One row per scenario across all feature areas, cross-referencing feature sheets for deep-dive config. Deliberately structured as merchant archetype plus trigger plus expected admin behaviour plus expected storefront output plus edge cases plus acceptance criteria so QA and dev read the same row.

nodes.label: FA-01 Tiered / Volume Pricing
nodes.rationale: Percentage or fixed discount by customer tag, scoped to all products, a collection, a product or a variant. Requires a customer tag and depends on Shopify Functions / Scripts.

nodes.label: FA-02 Quantity Breaks
nodes.rationale: Min/max quantity brackets with a discount per product or variant, delivered through cart transforms / Functions. Brackets must be non-overlapping, which is enforced as a save-time validation rather than resolved at pricing time.

nodes.label: FA-03 Fixed Price Rules
nodes.rationale: Overrides the Shopify base price outright for a tag+variant pair (used for negotiated contract prices), served via the Storefront API. Conflict policy is 'most specific rule wins'.

nodes.label: FA-04 Cart / Amount Discount
nodes.rationale: Evaluated on the cart subtotal after line-item pricing, with an explicit stacking config; interaction with Shopify native discount codes is flagged as needing a defined policy.

nodes.label: FA-05 B2B Registration Form
nodes.rationale: A workflow rather than a pricing rule: configurable fields, an approval step, and auto-tagging on approval, using the Customer API and email. Pricing only unlocks post-approval.

nodes.label: FA-06 Quick Order Form
nodes.rationale: Inherits whatever pricing rules are active rather than defining its own, so B2B prices show only for tagged customers. Capped at 50 products per order via Storefront / Cart API.

nodes.label: FA-07 Multi-Currency / Markets
nodes.rationale: Rules are authored in one base currency and Shopify Markets performs conversion, so the app never re-discounts a converted price; rounding is the known risk area and needs an explicit rounding rule.

nodes.label: FA-08 Tax Display (PDP Widget)
nodes.rationale: Display-only, zero pricing impact: renders ex-VAT and inc-VAT columns per tier row based on country, driven by the Tax API and geolocation. Regulatory driver is EU markets.

nodes.label: FA-09 CSV Bulk Import / Export
nodes.rationale: Admin tool with no customer-tag involvement; conflict resolution (overwrite/skip) is a configurable column-mapping concern and the CSV schema must be defined explicitly to keep imports reproducible.

nodes.label: FA-10 Manual Order Support
nodes.rationale: Pricing rules resolve on draft orders created by a rep in Shopify admin (Draft Order API) so offline deals price identically to storefront ones; a rep's manual override wins but must be logged for audit.

nodes.label: Merchant Archetypes Reference (MA-01..MA-07)
nodes.rationale: Seven archetypes (manufacturer, distributor, DTC-with-wholesale, trade-only, international, large catalogue, key account) exist to force realistic scenario coverage — each names the feature areas it needs so gaps in coverage become visible.

nodes.label: Acceptance Criteria Bank (AC-01..AC-19)
nodes.rationale: Reusable binary pass/fail statements with test input, expected output and owner, referenced by ID from the Scenario Master so criteria are written once and reused rather than restated per scenario.

nodes.label: Edge Cases Register (EC-01..EC-15)
nodes.rationale: Known edge cases carry a risk level and a linked scenario so sprint planning can triage them; several entries are explicitly 'must be defined/documented' rather than 'must be fixed'.

nodes.label: EC-01 Customer Holds Multiple Tags With Different Discounts
nodes.rationale: High risk. A customer tagged both 'wholesale' (10%) and 'vip' (20%) needs a deterministic winner — highest discount or most specific rule — and the choice must be documented, because silently picking one is the root of merchant-reported pricing disputes.
nodes.norm_label: ec-01 customer holds multiple tags with different discounts

nodes.label: EC-03 Overlapping Quantity Brackets
nodes.rationale: High risk. Brackets like 10-20 = 5% and 15-25 = 10% are rejected at save time rather than resolved at pricing time — pushing the ambiguity to configuration keeps the pricing path deterministic.

nodes.label: EC-07 Cart Discount Plus Shopify Native Discount Code
nodes.rationale: High risk. The stacking policy must be chosen explicitly — additive, highest wins, or block the code — because leaving it emergent lets margin leak through combined discounts.
nodes.norm_label: ec-07 cart discount plus shopify native discount code

nodes.label: EC-14 CSV Import Conflicts With Existing Rules
nodes.rationale: High risk. When an imported row targets a tag+SKU that already has a rule, the behaviour must be configurable (overwrite / skip / create duplicate) and documented — an undefined default silently corrupts a merchant's whole price book.
nodes.norm_label: ec-14 csv import conflicts with existing rules
