nodes.label: OSC Engineering Knowledge Base
nodes.rationale: PROJECT_STATUS.md answers what the system is and the code answers what it does; neither answers why it is built this way, which is the question that costs time.

nodes.label: Engineering Docs Are Not Part Of The Answer Corpus
nodes.rationale: An employee asking a product question must not be answered with the tracing design; the ingest root is docs/company/ only.
nodes.norm_label: engineering docs are not part of the answer corpus

nodes.label: Three Rules For Keeping Documentation Accurate
nodes.rationale: Drifted documentation is worse than none because it is trusted: same-commit updates, append-only ADRs, and every number carries the run it came from.
nodes.norm_label: three rules for keeping documentation accurate

nodes.label: Chunking And Embedding Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Documents are split because embedding windows are fixed, a whole-document vector is a vector for nothing in particular, and the prompt budget is finite.

nodes.label: Chunk Denormalises Title And Source URI
nodes.rationale: Deliberate redundancy so a retrieval hit is self-describing: generation can cite it without a second lookup and a non-SQL store need not support joins.
nodes.norm_label: chunk denormalises title and source uri

nodes.label: EmbeddedChunk Carries Its Embedding Model Id
nodes.rationale: A store can refuse to compare vectors produced by different models rather than silently returning nonsense similarity scores.
nodes.norm_label: embeddedchunk carries its embedding model id

nodes.label: Shared Chunk Id Helper And Idempotent Ingestion
nodes.rationale: One helper across chunkers keeps ingestion identical per strategy; the trap is that changing the chunker invalidates every chunk id while document hashes still match, leaving a stale index that looks healthy unless --reindex is used.
nodes.norm_label: shared chunk id helper and idempotent ingestion

nodes.label: recursive Chunking Strategy (default)
nodes.rationale: Splits on the coarsest separator that fits. Kept as default despite two known defects because switching changes every chunk id in a live index and a retrieval change ships with a measured improvement.

nodes.label: fixed Chunking Strategy
nodes.rationale: Deliberately naive fixed-size windows, retained as an evaluation control.

nodes.label: langchain_recursive Chunking Strategy
nodes.rationale: Same idea as recursive with better edge cases: no budget overshoot, no mid-word overlap cut.

nodes.label: markdown Chunking Strategy
nodes.rationale: Splits on heading structure first and records the heading path, so a question and its answer stay in one chunk. A hypothesis that must earn a number.

nodes.label: Chunk Size As The Highest-Leverage Knob
nodes.rationale: 900/120 sized against Qwen3's 4096-token window: ~225 tokens per chunk, five chunks of sources plus system prompt. Too small loses interpretability, too large dilutes the embedding.
nodes.norm_label: chunk size as the highest-leverage knob

nodes.label: Embedding Model Chosen Independently Of The Chat Model
nodes.rationale: Different jobs: an embedder is a retrieval instrument, a chat model is a writer. Coupling them would make a chat upgrade force a full re-index.
nodes.norm_label: embedding model chosen independently of the chat model

nodes.label: nomic-embed-text (768 dimensions)
nodes.rationale: Purpose-built for retrieval, runs locally so no corpus text leaves the host, and 768 sits inside pgvector's 2000-dimension HNSW limit.

nodes.label: Vector Dimension Fixed In The DDL / DimensionMismatchError
nodes.rationale: Failing loudly at startup is preferable to silently comparing incompatible vectors; changing the embedding model requires a new database and a full re-index.
nodes.norm_label: vector dimension fixed in the ddl / dimensionmismatcherror

nodes.label: Parsers Extract And Never Rewrite
nodes.rationale: Chunk text is quoted back as citation evidence, so invented or normalised text would make that evidence a forgery.

nodes.label: Unparseable Files Are Recorded As Failures, Not Deleted
nodes.rationale: Treating a file as present but unreadable stops a transient parse failure pruning a healthy document out of the index.
nodes.norm_label: unparseable files are recorded as failures, not deleted

nodes.label: Evaluation Harness
nodes.rationale: Before it every quality claim was an opinion and there was no way to find out which settings were wrong, so work stopped being cumulative.

nodes.label: Golden Set (86 cases)
nodes.rationale: Questions are phrased the way a user would ask them rather than copied from headings, because verbatim headings measure string matching and report it as retrieval quality.

nodes.label: Abstention Cases In The Golden Set
nodes.rationale: Without them an evaluation rewards a model that answers everything confidently — the exact failure this system is architected against.
nodes.norm_label: abstention cases in the golden set

nodes.label: Relevance Scored At Document Level
nodes.rationale: Chunk ids change with every chunker change, which would invalidate the golden set on precisely the experiment it exists to run. Document identity survives.

nodes.label: Golden-Set Path Guard Against The Index
nodes.rationale: A mistyped path and a genuine retrieval miss both score recall 0, and only one is a bug in the search stack.
nodes.norm_label: golden-set path guard against the index

nodes.label: recall@k
nodes.rationale: The headline metric: generation cannot recover from a passage never fetched, so recall bounds every downstream metric.

nodes.label: precision@k
nodes.rationale: Divides by k rather than by results returned, because unfilled slots were context the model could have had.

nodes.label: mrr
nodes.rationale: Measures ordering where recall measures presence.

nodes.label: hit_rate@k
nodes.rationale: Disambiguates a middling recall: every question partly answered, or some missed entirely.

nodes.label: groundedness
nodes.rationale: Computed from ids with set arithmetic: a citation whose chunk was not retrieved cannot have been read from a source. Needs no judge.

nodes.label: fact_match
nodes.rationale: Catches the local model's numeric-fidelity gap: right passage, right citation, wrong number.

nodes.label: citation_coverage / citation_precision
nodes.rationale: Catch a model answering without grounding, and citing something real but irrelevant.

nodes.label: abstention_accuracy
nodes.rationale: Hallucination on out-of-corpus questions.

nodes.label: LLM-As-Judge Faithfulness (opt-in)
nodes.rationale: Opt-in because it doubles model calls and measures with an instrument made of the same material; it uses fast_llm because judging a model with itself measures self-agreement. An unreachable judge records None, not a default.

nodes.label: Configuration Travels With The Numbers
nodes.rationale: A result JSON carries chunker, retrieval settings, reranker and both model ids so comparing two runs cannot silently compare two different systems.

nodes.label: A Failed Case Never Aborts The Run
nodes.rationale: A fragile harness does not get run, and one that averages a timeout in as zero teaches the team that the dashboard is noise.
nodes.norm_label: a failed case never aborts the run

nodes.label: Every Case Records Its Trace Id
nodes.rationale: Without it a bad number is the start of a reproduction rather than an explanation.
nodes.norm_label: every case records its trace id

nodes.label: An Absent Metric Is Not A Zero Metric
nodes.rationale: fact_match once scored 1.0 on retrieval-only runs because nothing was missing; omitting the keys also makes compare refuse a meaningless diff.
nodes.norm_label: an absent metric is not a zero metric

nodes.label: CI Gate via --fail-under
nodes.rationale: Parsed in the CLI rather than the runner because it is a policy about a run, not a property of one; deterministic metrics gate because a gate that changes its mind is not a gate.

nodes.label: Committed Baselines
nodes.rationale: Ad-hoc runs are noise; a run worth keeping is promoted to a named file because a baseline nobody can see is not a baseline.

nodes.label: What Evaluation Does Not Yet Measure
nodes.rationale: No hosted provider evaluated, scenario workbooks unscored, no user-written question, and nothing measures helpfulness.
nodes.norm_label: what evaluation does not yet measure

nodes.label: The Knowledge Corpus (docs/company/)
nodes.rationale: 21 documents, 193 chunks; the corpus root is the one boundary the assistant can retrieve from.

nodes.label: Corpus Boundary Enforced At Index Time
nodes.rationale: The failure mode is invisible: retrieval succeeds, generation is grounded, the citation is correct, and the answer is from the wrong universe. Nothing downstream catches it.
nodes.norm_label: corpus boundary enforced at index time

nodes.label: FAQ Split Into 17 Topic Files
nodes.rationale: A one-document corpus makes recall@5, precision@5 and MRR degenerate; the split also improves citation titles and gives chunks topically coherent neighbours.

nodes.label: Corpus Authoring Conventions
nodes.rationale: One topic per file, an H1 first line for the citation title, question-shaped headings, kebab-case filenames; no frontmatter, no index page, no manual document ids.

nodes.label: Uniform Access Control, Directory As The Boundary
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 was scoped to company-wide-readable content so per-document ACLs were not needed; when they land they resolve at index time and enforce as a SQL predicate.
nodes.norm_label: uniform access control, directory as the boundary

nodes.label: One Request, One Persistent Trace
nodes.rationale: Reproducing the request does not work because a generation is not deterministic: re-running produces a trace, not the trace.

nodes.label: trace.py — Context-Var Span Tree
nodes.rationale: A detached span outside a trace is why no code carries an `if tracing:` branch; nested traces extend rather than fork; ContextVar gives concurrent asyncio tasks clean traces.

nodes.label: store.py — Bounded Append-Only JSONL Log
nodes.rationale: Rotation not rewriting, because appending is O(1); writing never raises because instrumentation that can break what it observes is a liability.

nodes.label: render.py — Waterfall Renderer
nodes.rationale: Bars positioned by offset and sized by duration make 'these ran back to back' and 'this one dominated' distinguishable at a glance.

nodes.label: The Five-Step Debugging Workflow
nodes.rationale: doctor, traces --failed, trace <id>, search, chunk — each step narrows the next, and search separates 'misread the passage' from 'never retrieved it'.

nodes.label: A New Pipeline Stage Gets A Span
nodes.rationale: Attributes describe how the data changed — kept=12, discarded=18 is a fact you can act on; 'filtering candidates' is a sentence you already knew.
nodes.norm_label: a new pipeline stage gets a span

nodes.label: Instrument The Pipeline, Not The Adapter
nodes.rationale: Wrapping call sites covers all 37 providers at once and traces a new provider the day it is written; an adapter importing the tracer would be 37 places to keep consistent.
nodes.norm_label: instrument the pipeline, not the adapter

nodes.label: set_text As The Redaction Seam
nodes.rationale: capture_text: false reduces text to a length while retaining every timing, count and stage. A trace that cannot be sanitised is a trace that cannot be kept.

nodes.label: Structured Logging On stdlib logging
nodes.rationale: A JSON formatter is thirty lines and a dependency is forever.

nodes.label: Machine Output On stdout, Human Output On stderr
nodes.rationale: ./osc serve > run.log must still produce a clean parseable log while the terminal shows where the service is listening.
nodes.norm_label: machine output on stdout, human output on stderr

nodes.label: HTTP Trace Endpoints Gated On development
nodes.rationale: Not overridable by configuration, because traces carry question text and chunk ids and no endpoint on this service is authenticated yet.
nodes.norm_label: http trace endpoints gated on development

nodes.label: Traces Are Process-Local And Lossy
nodes.rationale: The log answers 'what happened recently, here', not 'across the fleet'; Span stays OTel-shaped so an exporter is an addition, not a rewrite.

nodes.label: OSC Architecture Overview
nodes.rationale: Almost every decision follows from two requirements pulling against each other: minimal hallucination and vendor agnosticism. Grounding solves the first, protocols the second.

nodes.label: The Request Path (rewrite → search → threshold → rerank → generate → cite)
nodes.norm_label: the request path (rewrite → search → threshold → rerank → generate → cite)

nodes.label: Abstention Is A Code Path, Not A Prompt Instruction
nodes.rationale: A prompt instruction is a request and a code path is a guarantee; no retrieval hits means the model is never called.
nodes.norm_label: abstention is a code path, not a prompt instruction

nodes.label: Citation Strength Differs By Provider, Silently
nodes.rationale: Anthropic returns citations verified against source text; every other provider has its [n] markers parsed back out. Both produce the same Citation shape, which is a known limitation rather than a claim of equivalence.
nodes.norm_label: citation strength differs by provider, silently

nodes.label: The Ingestion Path
nodes.rationale: Idempotent and incremental; an unreadable file is exempted from pruning because the difference between 'deleted at source' and 'temporarily unparseable' is the difference between a correct sync and permanent data loss.

nodes.label: Business Logic Imports protocols And types Only
nodes.rationale: The single rule that makes vendor agnosticism real rather than aspirational, and it is checkable with a grep.
nodes.norm_label: business logic imports protocols and types only

nodes.label: integrations/ May Import The Core; The Core May Never Import integrations/
nodes.rationale: That one-way edge stops an outbound adapter from becoming a dependency of the platform.
nodes.norm_label: integrations/ may import the core; the core may never import integrations/

nodes.label: Frozen Prompts
nodes.rationale: Module constants with no interpolation keep the prefix byte-identical, so prefix caching works and an evaluation score change is attributable to retrieval, not to the prompt.

nodes.label: Frozen Dataclasses For Domain Types
nodes.rationale: Domain values are constructed internally, so validation belongs at the trust boundary, not in the domain.

nodes.label: workspace_id From Day One
nodes.rationale: The only speculative design in the codebase, defended on one ground: adding a partition key to a populated corpus is a data migration, and not adding it is a column.

nodes.label: Operator Errors Are Messages; Bugs Are Tracebacks
nodes.rationale: AssistantError subclasses carry an actionable message; anything else keeps its frames, because for a bug the frames are the point.
nodes.norm_label: operator errors are messages; bugs are tracebacks

nodes.label: Where The Architecture Is Weakest
nodes.rationale: Stated openly because a knowledge base that only lists strengths is marketing: no auth, silent citation-strength difference, numeric misreads, process-local traces.

nodes.label: The Five Protocol Seams
nodes.rationale: Every model in this system will be replaced; the requirement was that switching providers requires configuration changes only.

nodes.label: VectorStore Protocol
nodes.rationale: The last change removed a method rather than adding one, and that direction is worth protecting: a protocol that keeps growing becomes a base class with extra steps.

nodes.label: StoreInspector Optional Protocol
nodes.rationale: Separate because a hosted vector database exposing no aggregate API should still be a perfectly good VectorStore; tooling probes with isinstance and reports its absence.

nodes.label: Protocols Rather Than Abstract Base Classes
nodes.rationale: The consequence that matters most: a test double is indistinguishable from a provider, so 'retargetable by configuration alone' is asserted by the test suite, not assumed.
nodes.norm_label: protocols rather than abstract base classes

nodes.label: Registry And Composition Root Wiring
nodes.rationale: The registry is populated as a side effect of one import at the composition root, so nothing in the call path imports every possible implementation.

nodes.label: Lazy cached_property Container Construction
nodes.rationale: ./osc ingest never constructs a chat model and therefore needs no LLM credential; the instance __dict__ is exactly the record of what was built, which gives shutdown its correctness property.

nodes.label: Container Injects Vector Width And Embedding Model Id
nodes.rationale: The store cannot know its own vector width, and the injection is what lets it refuse to compare vectors made by different models.
nodes.norm_label: container injects vector width and embedding model id

nodes.label: Two-Tier Provider Strategy
nodes.rationale: Native adapters keep provider-specific capabilities and are the default path; the LangChain bridge reaches the long tail at the cost of marker-parsed citations.

nodes.label: Never Let A Vendor Exception Escape An Adapter
nodes.rationale: Learned expensively: untranslated asyncpg exceptions surfaced as a bare OSError traceback in the CLI and bypassed the API error handler entirely.
nodes.norm_label: never let a vendor exception escape an adapter

nodes.label: Layered Configuration (env > .env > YAML profile)
nodes.rationale: Any value is addressable from the environment with OSC_ and __ nesting; ./osc config prints what actually resolved with credentials redacted.

nodes.label: Six-Stage Retrieval Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Generation cannot recover from a passage that was never fetched, so the stages are explicit and individually instrumented rather than compressed into a clever one-liner.

nodes.label: Hybrid Search (default)
nodes.rationale: Vector and keyword search have complementary blind spots and an internal corpus is dense with both, so choosing one means accepting a known failure mode on half the corpus. This is avoiding a known failure mode, not premature optimisation.

nodes.label: Vector Search
nodes.rationale: Handles paraphrase well and exact tokens badly: an embedder will place a fabricated identifier next to a real one.

nodes.label: Keyword Search (tsvector / BM25-equivalent)
nodes.rationale: Exactly the reverse of vector search: finds literal identifiers immediately, misses every paraphrase.

nodes.label: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k = 60)
nodes.rationale: Two ranked lists with incomparable scores cannot be merged by score, so RRF merges by rank — no normalisation, no tuned weight, nothing to recalibrate when the embedder changes.

nodes.label: Cormack, Clarke & Buettcher, Reciprocal Rank Fusion (SIGIR 2009)
nodes.norm_label: cormack, clarke & buettcher, reciprocal rank fusion (sigir 2009)

nodes.label: min_score Applied Before Reranking
nodes.rationale: Only first-stage scores are on a known scale; a cross-encoder logit is routinely negative for a relevant passage, so thresholding its output would discard the whole result set and present as 'the cross-encoder is useless'. A real defect, with a regression.

nodes.label: Cross-Encoder Reranking (off by default)
nodes.rationale: Strictly more informative and strictly more expensive; off because its value on OSC's corpus has never been measured.

nodes.label: Query Rewriting (off by default)
nodes.rationale: Best-effort by construction — a stage that can fail a request would be a liability since it is an optimisation. Off because it costs a call on the critical path, is unmeasured, and the bundled UI sends no history to rewrite from.

nodes.label: Measured Retrieval Baseline (recall@5 0.932)
nodes.rationale: precision@5 is low by construction because most cases have one relevant document out of five slots; the six missing cases cluster where the corpus genuinely overlaps.

nodes.label: Four Test Tiers
nodes.rationale: make test asks whether the system is correct; make eval asks whether it is good. A system can pass every test and answer every question badly.

nodes.label: In-Process Protocol Doubles In conftest.py
nodes.rationale: Deterministic bag-of-words embedder and scripted chat model registered through the ordinary registry, so the fast tier exercises the real pipelines with no network, database or credential.

nodes.label: Tests Never Touch The Production Corpus
nodes.rationale: A test asserting against docs/company/ would fail the day someone edited an FAQ answer — a false alarm and the fastest way to get a suite disabled. The rule was violated by test_e2e.py and repaired.
nodes.norm_label: tests never touch the production corpus

nodes.label: Tests Never Write Into The Working Directory
nodes.rationale: Trace persistence is on by default; redirecting per test also stops one test's traces making the next test's CLI assertions order-dependent.
nodes.norm_label: tests never write into the working directory

nodes.label: A Test Asserts A Behaviour, Not An Implementation
nodes.rationale: test_store_contract is parametrised over store implementations, so a new store is held to exactly the same behaviour.
nodes.norm_label: a test asserts a behaviour, not an implementation

nodes.label: A Found Defect Gets A Regression Test In The Same Commit
nodes.rationale: The highest-value category of test in the suite, which is why the bold rows are kept visible.
nodes.norm_label: a found defect gets a regression test in the same commit

nodes.label: Known Testing Gaps
nodes.rationale: No hosted provider ever called, no load test, an unreleasable Gemini HTTP client, a shared pgvector database, and no CI.

nodes.label: ADR 0001 — Five Protocols As The Swappability Seams
nodes.rationale: Vendor agnosticism was an explicit requirement, and it is in tension with 'avoid unnecessary abstractions'. Resolving that tension is what the decision is about: the number of protocols is five because five things are swapped.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0001 — five protocols as the swappability seams

nodes.label: Rejected: Abstract Base Classes And Framework Abstractions
nodes.rationale: ABCs would force third-party objects and test doubles to inherit from OSC's hierarchy; adopting a framework's abstractions would tie the domain model to its release cadence.
nodes.norm_label: rejected: abstract base classes and framework abstractions

nodes.label: Protocols Are Enforced Only Statically
nodes.rationale: Nothing at runtime checks a registered provider satisfies ChatModel, which makes mypy --strict load-bearing architecture rather than hygiene.

nodes.label: Provider-Specific Tuning Lives In Untyped options
nodes.rationale: A typed config per provider would put provider knowledge back in the settings schema.
nodes.norm_label: provider-specific tuning lives in untyped options

nodes.label: ADR 0002 — Adopt LangChain For Undifferentiated Work Only
nodes.rationale: The Phase 1 rejection was right about the framework and wrong about the libraries: what was treated as one decision was several, and two of the smaller ones deserved a different answer.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0002 — adopt langchain for undifferentiated work only

nodes.label: Adopt Where Undifferentiated, Keep OSC's Code Where OSC's Design Is Better
nodes.rationale: LangChain was refused wherever the component is either the thing OSC is actually good at or the thing that most needs to be readable.
nodes.norm_label: adopt where undifferentiated, keep osc's code where osc's design is better

nodes.label: langchain-core And langchain-text-splitters Are Core Dependencies
nodes.rationale: Both are pure Python with no vendor SDK behind them and both must be importable for the registries to be complete; every integration package stays an install-time choice.
nodes.norm_label: langchain-core and langchain-text-splitters are core dependencies

nodes.label: ADR 0003 — Hybrid Retrieval With RRF Fused In SQL
nodes.rationale: Retrieval bounds everything downstream, so the choice of method is the highest-consequence decision in the pipeline.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0003 — hybrid retrieval with rrf fused in sql

nodes.label: Rejected: Weighted Score Combination Instead Of RRF
nodes.rationale: It requires normalising cosine similarity against an unbounded ts_rank and then tuning a weight that would have to be re-derived every time the embedding model changed.
nodes.norm_label: rejected: weighted score combination instead of rrf

nodes.label: Rejected: Fusion In Application Code Over Two Queries
nodes.rationale: Two round trips, and ranking logic in the layer hardest to test against real data — the specific reason LangChain's PGVector was not adopted.
nodes.norm_label: rejected: fusion in application code over two queries

nodes.label: rrf_k = 60 Is Adopted On Authority, Not Tuned Here
nodes.rationale: The paper's value; never tuned on this corpus and probably should be now the harness exists.
nodes.norm_label: rrf_k = 60 is adopted on authority, not tuned here

nodes.label: min_score Is Nearly Useless In Hybrid Mode
nodes.rationale: An RRF score has no intuitive scale, so the threshold defaults to 0.0 and is effectively inert.
nodes.norm_label: min_score is nearly useless in hybrid mode

nodes.label: ADR 0004 — Persist Traces To A Bounded JSONL File
nodes.rationale: The in-memory ring buffer works for a long-lived server and not for the CLI, where the process exits the moment the answer is printed — so the situation in which a trace is most wanted was precisely the one in which there was none.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0004 — persist traces to a bounded jsonl file

nodes.label: Auto-Explain On Failure
nodes.rationale: A failed command prints its trace before the error, which needs no persistence at all.

nodes.label: Rejected: A traces Table In PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: It puts write load on the primary datastore for a debugging feature and makes tracing unavailable exactly when the database is what is broken.
nodes.norm_label: rejected: a traces table in postgresql

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry Exporter Deferred, Span Stays OTel-Shaped
nodes.rationale: The right destination once traces leave the host and the wrong answer for reading a trace in a terminal; keeping Span OTel-shaped makes the exporter an addition, not a rewrite.
nodes.norm_label: opentelemetry exporter deferred, span stays otel-shaped

nodes.label: Bounded Means Lossy — Not An Audit Log
nodes.rationale: Past max_trace_file_bytes x 2 old traces are gone: fine for a debugging aid, and it must never be mistaken for an audit log.
nodes.norm_label: bounded means lossy — not an audit log

nodes.label: ADR 0005 — An In-Repo Evaluation Harness, Not A Third-Party One
nodes.rationale: The rule 'a retrieval change ships with a measured improvement' was unenforceable and had already blocked a change that was probably correct.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0005 — an in-repo evaluation harness, not a third-party one

nodes.label: Rejected: RAGAS
nodes.rationale: LLM-judge-first, so the metrics that should gate CI are the non-deterministic ones; it would impose its data model on the code path we most want to read and pull in a second LLM abstraction. The metrics are twenty lines of set arithmetic.

nodes.label: Rejected: A pytest Suite With Quality Assertions
nodes.rationale: It conflates correctness with quality, and an assertion failing on ordinary model variance would get marked xfail within a week.
nodes.norm_label: rejected: a pytest suite with quality assertions

nodes.label: The Harness Drives The Real Pipelines
nodes.rationale: An evaluation that ran against a special code path would measure the special code path.
nodes.norm_label: the harness drives the real pipelines

nodes.label: The fact_match 1.0 Defect Found By Building It
nodes.rationale: A metric that was arithmetically correct and factually a lie; test_evaluation.py holds the regression.
nodes.norm_label: the fact_match 1.0 defect found by building it

nodes.label: A Golden Set Is A Maintained Asset
nodes.rationale: Edit an FAQ answer and a case may need updating; there is no way around it.
nodes.norm_label: a golden set is a maintained asset

nodes.label: ADR 0006 — Keep recursive As The Default Until Measured
nodes.rationale: Switching invalidates the entire index silently, and neither known defect has been shown to matter; 'probably right' is exactly the reasoning the measurement rule exists to replace.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0006 — keep recursive as the default until measured

nodes.label: A Retrieval Change Ships With A Measured Improvement
nodes.rationale: Adopting a change without a number would set the precedent that the rule applies only to other people's changes.
nodes.norm_label: a retrieval change ships with a measured improvement

nodes.label: fixed Retained As An Evaluation Control
nodes.rationale: A strategy that respects no structure at all says how much the structure-aware ones are actually worth.
nodes.norm_label: fixed retained as an evaluation control

nodes.label: Character-Based Rather Than Token-Based Sizing
nodes.rationale: Token sizing needs a tokenizer per model — a provider-specific dependency in the chunking layer, which is exactly the coupling the architecture avoids.

nodes.label: Semantic Chunking Deferred
nodes.rationale: Interesting, materially more expensive at ingest time, and unmeasurable against the same missing baseline. Deferred, not rejected.

nodes.label: The Open Chunker Comparison (Milestone A)
nodes.rationale: Whichever wins becomes the default, recorded as a superseding ADR; a decision that has been waiting on a measurement for two phases.

nodes.label: ADR 0007 — Corpus Root Is docs/company/; The FAQ Is Split By Topic
nodes.rationale: Two changes arrived together and collided: real company knowledge replaced the seed corpus, and the engineering knowledge base needed a home under docs/.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0007 — corpus root is docs/company/; the faq is split by topic

nodes.label: Rejected: An Ingest-Time Exclusion List
nodes.rationale: The directory boundary fails safe; an exclusion list fails open — more code, more config, and a mistake silently leaks internal documents into the answer index.

nodes.label: Rejected: Keep The FAQ As One File
nodes.rationale: Defensible on ingestion grounds and rejected on measurement grounds: it makes document-level retrieval metrics degenerate, and it produces worse citations.
nodes.norm_label: rejected: keep the faq as one file

nodes.label: Rejected: Split At Question Level (89 Files)
nodes.rationale: Retrieval would almost always need neighbouring questions, overlap would become meaningless, and a golden set naming one of 89 near-identical paths is harder to curate.
nodes.norm_label: rejected: split at question level (89 files)

nodes.label: The Corpus Root Is Named In Two Places
nodes.rationale: A Makefile variable and a CLI default that must agree; a single setting would be better.
nodes.norm_label: the corpus root is named in two places

nodes.label: openpyxl Added For .xlsx Scenario Workbooks
nodes.rationale: Two of the four scenario documents were otherwise invisible to the assistant; a third parsing library justified by real documents in the live corpus.

nodes.label: Provenance Edits Made During The Split
nodes.rationale: A subtitle line is the only corpus text not in the source, and two transcription typos were corrected and called out so they can be reverted.
nodes.norm_label: provenance edits made during the split

nodes.label: Architecture Decision Records
nodes.rationale: They prevent re-litigating settled questions and reversing a decision without knowing its cost. Several things look like omissions and are not.

nodes.label: ADRs Are Append-Only
nodes.rationale: Why a past decision was right at the time is itself information — it tells you which assumption changed.

nodes.label: Consequences Include The Costs
nodes.rationale: A record listing only benefits is advocacy, and nobody trusts it twice.

nodes.label: The Seven-Question Technology Page Format
nodes.rationale: Same seven questions on every page so they can be read in any order and compared.

nodes.label: Dependency Posture: Small Core, Vendor SDKs As Extras
nodes.rationale: A deployment installs only the SDKs for the providers it configures; logging.py is a thirty-line JSON formatter rather than a dependency, and that is the standard to argue against.
nodes.norm_label: dependency posture: small core, vendor sdks as extras

nodes.label: Three Questions Before Adding A Dependency
nodes.norm_label: three questions before adding a dependency

nodes.label: FastAPI
nodes.rationale: The pipeline is async end to end, streaming is first-class, Pydantic is already a dependency, and OpenAPI comes free for a service other teams will call.

nodes.label: Server-Sent Events Rather Than WebSockets
nodes.rationale: The traffic is one-directional, and SSE survives proxies, reconnects on its own and needs no protocol upgrade.

nodes.label: Lifespan Owns The Container
nodes.rationale: cached_property storing into the instance __dict__ means shutdown never constructs a component just to close it.

nodes.label: There Is No Write Endpoint
nodes.rationale: Ingestion is a CLI command, so the service exposes no unauthenticated way to modify the corpus — the only reason the current lack of authentication is merely bad rather than catastrophic.

nodes.label: Every SSE Exit Path Emits A Terminal Event
nodes.rationale: The handler once caught only AssistantError, so an unexpected exception closed the connection with no terminal event and left the UI spinning forever.
nodes.norm_label: every sse exit path emits a terminal event

nodes.label: No Authentication, Rate Limiting Or Concurrency Bound
nodes.rationale: The service says so at every non-development startup, but the constraint lives in prose rather than in the code path; the smallest fix is about ten lines and is a named milestone.
nodes.norm_label: no authentication, rate limiting or concurrency bound

nodes.label: response_model=None On /chat
nodes.rationale: Returning either JSON or a stream drops the JSON branch from the OpenAPI schema; splitting the endpoint is an API break the bundled UI would have to follow, deferred deliberately.

nodes.label: Graphify
nodes.rationale: Navigation without recursive reading, structural questions the code cannot answer, and — the underrated use — a check on the architecture: the graph is an outside observer and when it disagrees with the intended design it is usually right.

nodes.label: The StubEmbeddingModel Hub Finding
nodes.rationale: An earlier build reported a test double as the most connected node in the codebase — the graph's way of saying the test suite, not production wiring, exercised every seam. No architecture document would have surfaced it.

nodes.label: Graphify Caveats
nodes.rationale: The wiki/ output is stale, SQL migrations contribute no nodes without tree_sitter_sql, and docs/company/ is a corpus so a query can return an FAQ answer rather than code.

nodes.label: Ponytail
nodes.rationale: The handbook already says avoid unnecessary abstractions; Ponytail is that instruction made operational — a checklist that runs before code is written rather than a principle invoked during review when deleting feels like waste.

nodes.label: The Ponytail Ladder
nodes.rationale: Stop at the first rung that holds: YAGNI, already in the codebase, stdlib, native platform, installed dependency, one line, then minimum code.

nodes.label: Where Ponytail Is Deliberately Not Applied
nodes.rationale: Input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security and anything explicitly requested. Lazy at the core, strict at the edges.
nodes.norm_label: where ponytail is deliberately not applied

nodes.label: The ponytail: Comment Convention
nodes.rationale: A shortcut with a named upgrade path is a decision; an unmarked one is technical debt nobody remembers taking on.

nodes.label: LangChain
nodes.rationale: The most contested dependency in the project: rejected once, then partially adopted, and the reversal is recorded honestly.

nodes.label: langchain-text-splitters
nodes.rationale: Splitting on the coarsest boundary that fits is a genuinely generic problem, and heading-aware splitting would otherwise be written and maintained here.

nodes.label: langchain_bridge Provider Adapter
nodes.rationale: One adapter wraps any BaseChatModel or Embeddings behind OSC's protocols, making the long tail reachable by configuration rather than by writing an adapter each time.

nodes.label: Name The Class By Import Path, Not init_chat_model
nodes.rationale: init_chat_model lives in the langchain meta-package and would pull LangGraph in to save one line of configuration.
nodes.norm_label: name the class by import path, not init_chat_model

nodes.label: OSC Exposed As A LangChain BaseRetriever
nodes.rationale: The reasoning is organisational: OSC's value is the index, and teams building on frameworks OSC does not control would otherwise stand up a parallel index that drifts.
nodes.norm_label: osc exposed as a langchain baseretriever

nodes.label: What LangChain Was Refused
nodes.rationale: Vector store, retrieval pipeline, answer loop, prompts, tracing and the document type — refused wherever the component is what OSC is good at or what most needs to be readable.

nodes.label: Ollama
nodes.rationale: No corpus text leaves the host, no credential, and zero marginal cost per run — free evaluation is evaluation that actually happens.

nodes.label: Reached Through The openai_compatible Adapter
nodes.rationale: Ollama shares the twelve-name family, so the same adapter serves Groq, Together, Fireworks, vLLM and a local llama.cpp server.

nodes.label: qwen3:8b
nodes.rationale: Reasoning disabled: 138 completion tokens with thinking versus 3 without, and thinking competes with the answer inside a 4096-token context where an exhausted budget returns empty content.

nodes.label: nomic-embed-text
nodes.rationale: 768 dimensions, purpose-built for retrieval rather than a generative model's hidden states, chosen independently of the chat model.

nodes.label: The Numeric-Fidelity Gap
nodes.rationale: qwen3:8b rendered '500 to 2,500 EUR' as '50,000 to 2,500 EUR' while citing the correct passage — what fact_match exists to quantify rather than anecdote.

nodes.label: Citations Are Asserted, Not Verified
nodes.rationale: A deliberate trade for vendor agnosticism, and a gap that should be measured.

nodes.label: 4096-Token Context Caps The Corpus Per Answer
nodes.rationale: A question needing six passages is answered incompletely rather than incorrectly — the better of the two failure modes, but still a failure.
nodes.norm_label: 4096-token context caps the corpus per answer

nodes.label: PostgreSQL + pgvector
nodes.rationale: It is boring: every team knows how to back it up, monitor it and restore it at 3am, and a dedicated vector database would buy nothing at this corpus size.

nodes.label: One Datastore Holds Everything
nodes.rationale: A chunk and its vector cannot drift apart, there is one backup, and hybrid retrieval is one round trip.

nodes.label: Conditional HNSW Index (dimension <= 2000)
nodes.rationale: Above pgvector's limit search degrades to an exact scan, so the migration reports which path it took rather than failing.

nodes.label: search_vector Is A Generated Column
nodes.rationale: The lexical index cannot fall out of sync with the text because there is no application code that could forget to update it.

nodes.label: SQL-Side RRF Fusion (two CTEs)
nodes.rationale: fusion.py holds the same formula in Python for the memory store, so both stores rank identically and the in-memory store is a legitimate test double for ranking.

nodes.label: workspace_id On Every Table
nodes.rationale: Adding a partition key to a populated corpus is a data migration; not adding it is a column.

nodes.label: asyncpg Errors Translated To VectorStoreError
nodes.rationale: Untranslated they surfaced as a bare OSError traceback in the CLI and bypassed the API's error handler entirely, with the DSN password unredacted.

nodes.label: Ingestion Assumes A Single Writer
nodes.rationale: _prune reads the hash map at the start of a sync and deletes anything absent at the end, so two concurrent ingestions would fight.

nodes.label: One Database Is One Failure Domain
nodes.rationale: Precisely why the trace log is a file and not a table: the debugging tool must survive the thing it debugs.
nodes.norm_label: one database is one failure domain

nodes.label: Pydantic At Every Trust Boundary, And Nowhere Else
nodes.rationale: HTTP requests, settings and golden-set YAML parse untrusted input; domain types are constructed internally, so per-instantiation validation would be cost with no benefit.
nodes.norm_label: pydantic at every trust boundary, and nowhere else

nodes.label: Four-Layer Settings Precedence
nodes.rationale: A custom PydanticBaseSettingsSource; test_settings.py pins the precedence in ten tests, added after the module was found to have none.

nodes.label: Typer And Rich CLI
nodes.rationale: The signature is the interface, so options, types, defaults and help cannot drift; the waterfall is the difference between reading timings and seeing which stage dominated.

nodes.label: Flat Command Surface With Three --help Panels
nodes.rationale: Sub-command nesting costs typing on every invocation and buys grouping that fifteen commands do not need; --help is the discovery surface.
nodes.norm_label: flat command surface with three --help panels

nodes.label: ruff
nodes.rationale: Replaces flake8, isort, pyupgrade, pydocstyle and several plugins with one tool and one config block, fast enough to run on every save.

nodes.label: mypy --strict As Load-Bearing Architecture
nodes.rationale: A Protocol is only enforced statically, so strict typing is what turns 'satisfies the protocol' from a convention into a check; without it the central architectural claim would be unverified.

nodes.label: pytest With asyncio_mode = auto
nodes.rationale: Nearly every function is a coroutine; requiring a decorator on 300 tests would be noise.

nodes.label: hatchling Build Backend
nodes.rationale: PEP 517/621 compliant with no setup.py, and it force-includes py.typed so consumers see the annotations.

nodes.label: The ./osc Wrapper Script
nodes.rationale: A path into a virtualenv in documentation is a path that is wrong on someone else's machine, and it is wrong silently.

nodes.label: documents Extra (pypdf, python-docx, openpyxl)
nodes.rationale: Markdown, text, reStructuredText and HTML need nothing beyond the standard library, so a Markdown-only deployment should not install three parsing libraries.

nodes.label: Engineering Philosophy
nodes.rationale: Software must be correct, reliable, understandable, maintainable, extensible and documented. Code quality outranks implementation speed because the system is expected to remain readable for years; prefer the simpler solution when it does not sacrifice future extensibility.

nodes.label: Optimisation Priority Order
nodes.rationale: Correctness > reliability > maintainability > readability > scalability > performance > development speed. An explicit ordering exists so trade-off arguments resolve against a stated rule rather than per-author taste; premature optimisation is rejected on the same grounds.

nodes.label: Operational Tooling (./osc CLI)
nodes.rationale: The tooling exists so the common questions have answers that cannot go stale — read the tool output before reading source. `./osc` deliberately runs the CLI without a .venv path, so no command, Makefile target or doc ever hardcodes a virtualenv path.

nodes.label: Failure Diagnosis Workflow
nodes.rationale: doctor -> traces --failed -> trace <id> -> search -> chunk, in that order because each step narrows the next. `search` in particular separates 'the model misread the passage' from 'the passage was never retrieved' — different bugs, different fixes.

nodes.label: Measurement Rules — a retrieval change ships with a number
nodes.rationale: Chunk size, top_k, rrf_k, chunker, reranker and query rewriting are all educated guesses; moving one without a before/after number is how the guesses became permanent. Deterministic metrics gate CI and the LLM judge is opt-in, because a gate that can change its mind between two runs of the same commit is not a gate. Compare with --baseline, never by eye. --reindex after a chunker change, or an ordinary sync silently measures the old index under the new label.
nodes.norm_label: measurement rules — a retrieval change ships with a number

nodes.label: Knowledge Corpus Rules — docs/company is the corpus
nodes.rationale: docs/engineering/ must never be indexed: an answer sourced from an ADR would retrieve cleanly, ground correctly and cite accurately while being from the wrong universe, and nothing downstream catches it. Tests use isolated fixtures because a test asserting against a real FAQ answer fails the day someone edits it.
nodes.norm_label: knowledge corpus rules — docs/company is the corpus

nodes.label: Observability Rules for New Code
nodes.rationale: A new pipeline stage gets a span with data-shaped attributes, not prose. Instrument the pipeline, not the adapter — adapters stay pure translation and wrapping the call site covers every provider at once. Anything derived from a document or user goes through set_text, which is the seam capture_text:false switches off. Instrumentation must never raise, because a tracer that can break the thing it observes is a liability precisely because it is trusted.

nodes.label: Output Rules — stdout/stderr split and error hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Machine-readable output to stdout, human-readable to stderr, so `./osc serve > run.log` still yields a parseable log. Operator problems are AssistantError messages; bugs keep their tracebacks because for a bug the frames are the point. A vendor exception must never escape a provider adapter or the layers above cannot handle it.
nodes.norm_label: output rules — stdout/stderr split and error hierarchy

nodes.label: Session Startup Checklist
nodes.rationale: Read PROJECT_STATUS.md, README.md, docs/engineering/ and graphify-out/, then run ./osc doctor before suspecting the code — most surprises come from outside the process. Navigate by the generated graph rather than reading the repository recursively.

nodes.label: OSC Engineering Handbook (claude.md)
nodes.rationale: Byte-identical to AGENTS.md apart from the title heading; it is the repository's engineering standards document, cited by PROJECT_STATUS.md as the source of the project's stated priorities and optimisation order.

nodes.label: Vendor Agnosticism
nodes.rationale: Chat model, embedding model, reranker, vector store and chunker are each selected by configuration and swappable independently. The enforcing rule is that business logic imports only `protocols` and `types` and never a provider module — a rule chosen because it is checkable with a grep, which is what makes the property real rather than aspirational.

nodes.label: The Five Protocol Seams
nodes.rationale: ChatModel, EmbeddingModel, VectorStore, Reranker and Chunker are Protocols satisfied structurally — no base class, no inheritance — so a test double is indistinguishable from a provider, which is what makes the API and CLI tests meaningful.

nodes.label: StoreInspector — optional inspection protocol
nodes.rationale: Kept deliberately out of VectorStore: every VectorStore method is one a new store must implement to be usable at all, whereas a hosted vector database exposing no aggregate API should still be a perfectly good VectorStore. Tooling probes with isinstance and reports absence rather than failing.

nodes.label: Container — composition root and lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Builds components lazily via cached_property, so `ingest` never constructs a chat model and therefore never needs an LLM credential. Shutdown releases exactly what was built, because cached_property's presence in __dict__ is itself the record of construction; components are probed for aclose/close rather than required to have one.

nodes.label: Registry wiring — providers as plug-in additions
nodes.rationale: Five Registry instances map provider name to factory; a provider module registers itself on import and nothing in the call path imports every possible implementation. Adding a provider is a new file plus one import line rather than an edit to business logic.
nodes.norm_label: registry wiring — providers as plug-in additions

nodes.label: Hybrid Retrieval
nodes.rationale: Internal corpora are dense with acronyms, codenames and error strings that semantic search handles badly, and paraphrase that keyword search handles badly. Postgres provides both indexes, so the marginal cost is one query plus fusion. Avoiding a known failure mode, not premature optimisation.

nodes.label: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)
nodes.rationale: Implemented identically in fusion.py and in SQL inside the pgvector store so both stores rank identically; the SQL implementation fuses lexical and vector search in one round trip, which is the measurable capability LangChain's PGVector would have cost. rrf_k is still the SIGIR paper's value, adopted on authority and never tuned for this corpus.

nodes.label: Architectural Abstention
nodes.rationale: No retrieval hits means the model is never called; no citations means the answer is treated as ungrounded. Architectural rather than a prompt instruction, so it is a guarantee. In streaming mode the final `complete` event is authoritative. The prose self-abstention a model may write is a behaviour with no guarantee behind it, and abstention_accuracy currently cannot distinguish the two mechanisms.

nodes.label: Observability Layer (trace / store / render)
nodes.rationale: Three modules with one dependency direction — trace collects, store persists, render presents — composed only in the package __init__. span() outside a trace returns a detached span that records nothing, so instrumented code carries no `if tracing` branches; trace() nested inside another trace extends rather than forks, which is what lets `retrieve` be both a whole operation and a stage of one.

nodes.label: Bounded append-only JSONL trace log
nodes.rationale: Chosen over re-running with --explain (a generation is not deterministic, so you get a trace, not the trace), a traces table in PostgreSQL (write load on the primary datastore, and unavailable exactly when the database is what broke), OpenTelemetry with a collector (right destination once traces leave the host, wrong answer for reading one in a terminal), and a daemon (worse than the problem). The file is the smallest thing that outlives a process, needs no service or migration, and reuses the payload the HTTP endpoint already serves.

nodes.label: Evaluation Framework
nodes.rationale: Built in-repo rather than adopting RAGAS/TruLens/DeepEval: each is LLM-judge-first so the metrics that should gate CI are the non-deterministic ones, each imposes its own data model on the code path most in need of reading, and the metrics themselves are twenty lines of set arithmetic. It drives the real pipelines built by the real Container, because an evaluation against a special code path would measure the special code path. Relevance is scored at document level because chunk ids derive from chunk boundaries, so chunker changes would otherwise invalidate the golden set on exactly the experiment it exists to run. Groundedness is computed from ids, not judgement.

nodes.label: Measured Quality Baseline (recall@5 0.932, mrr 0.860)
nodes.rationale: Committed to evaluation/baselines/ so a regression fails CI, and so two runs cannot silently compare two different systems — every result carries a configuration snapshot. precision@5 of 0.190 is not alarming: most cases have exactly one relevant document out of five slots, so 0.2 is the ceiling; it is a relative measure across runs, misleading as an absolute.

nodes.label: fact_match reported 1.0 for work never done
nodes.rationale: Computed as 'no expected fact was missing', so a --retrieval-only run that generated no answers had missed nothing — arithmetically correct, factually a lie. Fixed by omitting generation metrics entirely from a retrieval-only run: a metric that is absent is not a metric that is zero. Recorded because it is the class of bug an evaluation subsystem is most prone to.
nodes.norm_label: fact_match reported 1.0 for work never done

nodes.label: Corpus / engineering-docs directory split
nodes.rationale: The ingest root moved from docs/ to docs/company/ because an employee asking 'how does OSC handle refunds?' could have been answered from an ADR about reciprocal rank fusion, with a correct citation, confidently — retrieval succeeds, grounding succeeds, the citation is right, the universe is wrong. An exclusion list would fail open; a directory boundary fails safe. The root is named in exactly two places (Makefile DOCS and the --corpus default) and they must agree.

nodes.label: 633-line FAQ split into 17 topic files
nodes.rationale: All 89 questions preserved verbatim. The reason is measurement, not presentation: with a single-document corpus recall@k is 1.0 for every answerable question and the retrieval metrics measure nothing. Citations improved from 'Advance FAQ' to 'Tax Display' as a side effect.

nodes.label: Scoped LangChain Integration
nodes.rationale: Rule applied: adopt LangChain for undifferentiated work, keep OSC's own code where OSC's design is better. Adopted for text splitting, provider reach via a bridge adapter, and outbound interoperability as a BaseRetriever. Not adopted for the vector store (SQL RRF in one round trip), the retrieval pipeline (LCEL would obscure the path most in need of reading), the answer loop, prompts or tracing. langchain-core and langchain-text-splitters are core deps because both are pure Python with no vendor SDK; every integration package stays an install-time choice named in options.class_path.

nodes.label: Citation strength differs by provider, silently
nodes.rationale: Anthropic returns citations verified against source text; every other provider — including the local default and the LangChain bridge — asserts them via [n] markers a model can emit for an unsupported claim. Both produce the same Citation shape, so nothing downstream can tell the difference. A deliberate trade-off for vendor agnosticism; the gap is meant to be measured, and citation_precision 0.732 against groundedness 1.00 is what indiscriminate citation of all five sources looks like.
nodes.norm_label: citation strength differs by provider, silently

nodes.label: Frozen Prompts
nodes.rationale: System prompts are module constants with no interpolation. Anything dynamic would break prefix caching for every request and make evaluation results unattributable. A template engine has nothing to add to a constant.

nodes.label: Operator errors are messages; bugs are tracebacks
nodes.rationale: AssistantError is the project's vocabulary for problems an operator must fix, each carrying an actionable message. A traceback buries that under frames describing our call stack rather than their problem. Anything else keeps its frames, because for a bug the frames are the point. Untranslated asyncpg errors previously surfaced as a bare OSError and bypassed the API error handler entirely — the most common operational failure was also the worst reported.
nodes.norm_label: operator errors are messages; bugs are tracebacks

nodes.label: workspace_id partition key from day one
nodes.rationale: The only speculative design in the codebase, and defended on the grounds that adding a partition key to an already-populated corpus is a data migration.
nodes.norm_label: workspace_id partition key from day one

nodes.label: latency_p95 of 92.9 s against a 120 s provider timeout
nodes.rationale: Measured under --concurrency 2 against a single Ollama instance, so partly contention and partly cold start; the slowest case took 223 s for 197 output tokens. Observed p95 is within a factor of 1.3 of the point where requests start failing rather than merely being slow, and nothing caps concurrency today.
nodes.norm_label: latency_p95 of 92.9 s against a 120 s provider timeout

nodes.label: Two scenario workbooks are 42% of the index
nodes.rationale: 82 of 193 chunks come from two .xlsx files and compete for retrieval slots against the FAQ; four of six recall failures retrieved a spreadsheet chunk in place of the answering FAQ document. Whether that is bad chunking of tabular data, bad ranking, or a golden set that under-specifies its relevant documents is undetermined — and is exactly the kind of question the harness now makes answerable.
nodes.norm_label: two scenario workbooks are 42% of the index

nodes.label: Local answer model misreads figures
nodes.rationale: qwen3:8b rendered '500 to 2,500 EUR' as '50,000 to 2,500 EUR' while citing the correct passage — retrieval right, citation right, number wrong. The central honest caveat of the local stack, bounded further by a 4096-token context that caps sources at five chunks.

nodes.label: Knowledge-graph structural observations
nodes.rationale: 2086 nodes / 4572 edges / 131 communities. MemoryVectorStore, Document, ComponentConfig and Container are the architectural hubs, matching intended design. An earlier build reported StubEmbeddingModel — a test double — as the single most connected node, the graph's way of saying the test suite rather than production wiring exercised every seam. graphify-out/wiki/ is stale; the graph itself is current.

nodes.label: Milestone A′ — Spend the Harness
nodes.rationale: No new code. A recorded chunker decision (recursive vs langchain_recursive vs markdown), a reranker decision, a top_k/rrf_k decision, one hosted-provider run, and the spreadsheet-chunk question answered. The binding constraint has moved: measurement was item 1 for three phases, now exists, and everything it gated is unblocked at once.

nodes.label: Milestone B — Authentication (OIDC)
nodes.rationale: The first hard blocker to exposing the service; group membership from the IdP is also the input to per-document ACLs. Includes a production start-up guard — refuse to start when environment != development and no auth is configured — so the constraint becomes enforced rather than announced.

nodes.label: Milestone C — Retrieval Quality Pass
nodes.rationale: Requires the harness. Every change carries a before/after number, and anything that did not move a metric is reverted. Includes a recorded decision on the cross-encoder reranker and on query rewriting — kept with a measured improvement, or defaulted off and the fast_llm dependency removed.

nodes.label: Milestone D — Deployment and Export
nodes.rationale: Dockerfile, CI running make check and make eval-gate, and an OTel exporter behind a configuration flag with the local trace log retained as default — Span is deliberately OTel-shaped so that day is an exporter rather than a rewrite.

nodes.label: CLI Command Surface (running / understanding / looking at data)
nodes.rationale: Commands are grouped by purpose in --help rather than listed flat, and every inspection command takes --json so they compose into scripts.
nodes.norm_label: cli command surface (running / understanding / looking at data)

nodes.label: --explain trace waterfall
nodes.rationale: Answers where the time went, what each stage did to the data, and which stage failed, without a log line or a debugger. An abstention is visible by shape — a trace with retrieve and no generate means the model was never called. Streaming records time to first token separately because for a streaming client that is the number describing the experience. Every answer carries its trace_id so 'this answer is wrong' stays answerable hours later.

nodes.label: Idempotent ingestion by content hash
nodes.rationale: Re-running over an unchanged corpus makes zero embedding calls; an edited file re-indexes alone and a deleted file is pruned with its chunks. One bad file cannot break a sync — a corrupt document is reported and skipped, the command exits non-zero, and crucially it is not pruned, because a file that failed to parse is still present at the source.

nodes.label: --reindex escape hatch
nodes.rationale: The content hash covers the document text and nothing else, so changing chunking.strategy, chunk_size or the embedding model leaves every stored chunk stale while every hash still matches. An ordinary sync would report `skipped` for the whole corpus and quietly keep the old chunks.

nodes.label: Multi-format text extraction
nodes.rationale: Markdown/text byte-for-byte, HTML via the standard library, PDF via pypdf, .docx via python-docx including table cells, .xlsx via openpyxl with cells tab-joined so a row survives as one line. Adding a format is a function plus one dict entry; nothing else changes. Scanned PDFs are rejected with an explicit message rather than indexed as empty documents.

nodes.label: Layered configuration (env > .env > YAML profile)
nodes.rationale: Any value is addressable from the environment with OSC_ and a double underscore for nesting. `./osc config` prints what was actually resolved alongside the OSC_* variables that participated — the fast answer to 'production is using the wrong model' — with credentials redacted unless --show-secrets.

nodes.label: Experiment profiles
nodes.rationale: Copy a profile, change one thing, point OSC_PROFILE at it. hosted-anthropic moves every component to a hosted vendor and is the only configuration with provider-verified citations; local-only swaps in sentence-transformers and the cross-encoder; groq-voyage shares no vendor with either; langchain-bridge reaches a provider through LangChain with heading-aware chunking. None requires a code change.

nodes.label: min_score applies before reranking
nodes.rationale: First-stage scores are on a known scale; a cross-encoder logit is unbounded and often negative for a relevant passage. Thresholding reranker output would have emptied the result set the moment a reranker was enabled.

nodes.label: One datastore (PostgreSQL)
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL holds chunk text, embeddings, the lexical index and document metadata, so a chunk and its vector cannot drift apart, there is one backup to take, and hybrid retrieval is one round trip. A dedicated vector database earns its place when vector search p95 degrades or the corpus passes a few million chunks — the VectorStore protocol is where that swap happens.

nodes.label: Tracing is OSC's own, not OpenTelemetry and not LangChain callbacks
nodes.rationale: OTel is the right answer once traces leave the process, and observability/trace.py is deliberately shaped like it — spans, parent ids, attributes — so that day is an exporter rather than a rewrite; today it would add a large dependency and a collector for a capability that fits in one file. LangChain callbacks were rejected for a stronger reason: they observe only LangChain runs, so a tracer built on them would be blind to chunking, pgvector's SQL fusion and the abstention decision — exactly the parts most in need of debugging.
nodes.norm_label: tracing is osc's own, not opentelemetry and not langchain callbacks

nodes.label: Working with a reasoning model (Qwen3)
nodes.rationale: The default profile disables reasoning because Ollama loads the model with a 4096-token context and reasoning competes with the answer for that budget. chunk_size, top_k and max_tokens are all sized to fit the same window. Re-enabling reasoning requires raising max_tokens; an exhausted budget produces no answer text at all, and the adapter reports that explicitly rather than letting it become a silent 'I could not find anything'.

nodes.label: Evaluation commands and published baseline
nodes.rationale: make test asks whether the system is correct; make eval asks whether it is good — different questions, and a system can pass every test while answering every question badly, which is why evaluation is a command and not a test file. Comparison prints per-metric deltas and every configuration key that differs, so two runs of different systems cannot be mistaken for a result. --judge is opt-in.

nodes.label: Server output split by audience (stderr banner, stdout JSON)
nodes.rationale: `./osc serve > run.log` still produces a clean parseable log while the terminal stays readable. The startup note about an empty index earns its place: a service which starts perfectly and abstains from every question is indistinguishable from a broken model unless somebody thinks to look.
nodes.norm_label: server output split by audience (stderr banner, stdout json)

nodes.label: Default profile — fully local stack
nodes.rationale: Nothing in this configuration sends corpus text or questions off the host and no API credential is required. Every value is overridable with OSC_ and a double underscore; running an experiment is copying the file, changing what is tested and pointing OSC_PROFILE at the copy — no code change, no rebuild.

nodes.label: reasoning_effort: none for Qwen3
nodes.rationale: Measured on this deployment: 138 completion tokens with thinking versus 3 without, for the same reply. Off for two reasons — Ollama's 4096-token context means thinking competes with the answer and an exhausted budget returns empty content, and grounded QA over retrieved passages is mostly extractive so the latency is not repaid. include_usage_in_stream is set because Ollama reports usage only on the final stream chunk, and without it the streaming path records zero tokens for every request.

nodes.label: Chunking settings — recursive, 900/120
nodes.rationale: Sized against the answer model's 4096-token context: roughly 225 tokens per chunk, five chunks of sources, leaving room for the system prompt and the answer. Raise both if the model is served with a larger context.

nodes.label: Retrieval settings — hybrid, 30 candidates, top_k 5, rrf_k 60
nodes.norm_label: retrieval settings — hybrid, 30 candidates, top_k 5, rrf_k 60

nodes.label: Query rewriting off by default
nodes.rationale: It resolves follow-up references but costs a second model call on the critical path, and its benefit has never been measured against a golden set. Enable it together with an evaluation run.

nodes.label: noop reranker by default
nodes.rationale: Reranking is off until the evaluation harness can show the gain on OSC's own golden set. Switching to cross_encoder is safe now that min_score is applied to first-stage scores, so enabling a reranker no longer risks discarding everything.

nodes.label: Embedding choice fixes the vector width
nodes.rationale: Chosen independently of the answer model. Changing it changes the vector width and therefore requires a full re-index against a fresh chunks table. nomic-embed-text is a purpose-built retrieval embedder at 768 dimensions, comfortably inside pgvector's 2000-dimension HNSW index limit.
nodes.norm_label: embedding choice fixes the vector width

nodes.label: Observability settings (buffer, span cap, persistence, capture_text)
nodes.rationale: trace_buffer_size answers 'what did that request just do?', not 'what happened last Tuesday' — durable traces belong in a collector. max_spans_per_trace bounds a corpus-wide ingestion while totals stay accurate past the cap. persist_traces exists because a one-shot CLI trace is gone the moment it exits and re-running does not reproduce a non-deterministic generation. capture_text:false retains every timing, count and stage and reduces text to a character count. expose_traces additionally requires environment == development, and that check is deliberately not overridable here.
nodes.norm_label: observability settings (buffer, span cap, persistence, capture_text)

nodes.label: LangChain bridge experiment profile
nodes.rationale: The point of the profile is what is not in it: no new adapter, no code change, no entry in a provider table — a LangChain integration package plus three lines of configuration, and hybrid retrieval, RRF, citations, abstention and tracing all run unchanged on top of it. Anthropic is used only because it is easy to verify; in practice the native adapter is better for it because it returns citations verified against the source text while the bridge parses [n] markers. Reach for the bridge when there is no native adapter — Bedrock, Vertex, Azure, Cohere, Mistral, Fireworks, Databricks.

nodes.label: Heading-aware markdown chunking
nodes.rationale: Sections split on structure first and packed to size second, each chunk recording the heading path it sits under. Changing the chunker changes every chunk boundary and therefore every chunk id, which the content hash does not cover — so this profile needs its own database and a --reindex.

nodes.label: Embeddings held local in the bridge experiment
nodes.rationale: Embeddings stay on Ollama because they are chosen independently of the chat model and this experiment is about the chat bridge — swapping them would confuse two variables.
nodes.norm_label: embeddings held local in the bridge experiment

nodes.label: OSC Golden Set (86 cases)
nodes.rationale: 81 curated questions across seventeen FAQ topic areas plus 5 abstention cases. relevant_documents are corpus-relative paths under the ingest root docs/company.

nodes.label: Questions phrased as a merchant would ask them
nodes.rationale: A golden set of verbatim FAQ headings measures string matching and reports it as retrieval quality — every question would score 1.0 and the number would move for no reason anyone could act on.
nodes.norm_label: questions phrased as a merchant would ask them

nodes.label: expected_facts curation rule
nodes.rationale: Facts are short, distinctive and load-bearing — a number, a limit, a tag, a product name. Anything longer scores the model's phrasing rather than its correctness and would fail a perfectly good answer that used a synonym.

nodes.label: Document-level relevance labels
nodes.rationale: relevant_documents name corpus-relative paths rather than chunk ids, so the labels survive a chunker change — the experiment the golden set exists to run.

nodes.label: Abstention case set (must_abstain)
nodes.rationale: Five questions the corpus genuinely cannot answer — pricing plans, refund policy, WooCommerce/BigCommerce compatibility, API rate limits, employee annual leave. Deliberate, because without them an evaluation rewards a model that answers everything, which is the failure mode this system is designed against.

nodes.label: OSCP Wholesale B2B FAQ corpus (17 topic files)
nodes.rationale: Seventeen faq/*.md topic files — tiered pricing, offer priority, product/collection integration, theme compatibility, tax display, market, order limits, row-level discount, cart discount, combined collection slabs, add-on tier pricing, extra fee, export, quick order form, registration form, free gift, draft order — are the documents the golden set labels as relevant.
nodes.norm_label: oscp wholesale b2b faq corpus (17 topic files)
